findings.reason: A nonempty Profile description is submitted but is absent after reload and the Edit description field is blank.
findings.nextAction: Investigate Profile create/update DTO and storage/read mapping; retain the persisted-description assertion.

findings.reason: The deployed Profile delete action sends the owned UUID and returned HTTP 500. This is not a successful cleanup.
findings.nextAction: Fix the application delete contract/handler. Track owned leftover records; do not automatically repeat failed deletes.

findings.reason: The deployed Features panel exposes a table and selected tab; the old test demanded a nonexistent Manage Features heading.
findings.nextAction: Verify the selected Features panel and table.

findings.reason: The deployed forms validate required fields on Save. Old disabled-button and boolean-type assertions did not verify the functional outcome.
findings.nextAction: Require visible validation or prevented Save, an unchanged form, and no invalid server write.

findings.reason: Controlled 403, 404, and 500 delete rejections preserve the record but display no visible error notification. These checks did not send real DELETE requests to the server.
findings.nextAction: Add visible failure feedback or confirm the required error UX; these client-handling checks do not prove server authorization enforcement.

findings.reason: Clearing the optional maintenance date leaves the prior date in the saved license after reload.
findings.nextAction: Fix the deployed save mapping so an explicit clear persists a null maintenance date; retain the clearing assertion.

findings.reason: Feature create submits a nonempty description and Standard access level, but both are absent in fresh GET data and the reopened Edit form. Version 1.0.0 persists.
findings.nextAction: Investigate Feature create/update/read mapping for description and access levels; retain the persisted-value checks.

findings.reason: The owned Feature DELETE by the UUID used by the deployed UI returned HTTP 200, but the same record remains in fresh GET data and the UI.
findings.nextAction: Fix the deletion contract or persistence; the owned leftover is documented and should not be repeatedly deleted automatically.

findings.reason: Old configuration tests selected the first leaf group, which was empty. Live data contained 142 configurations across 47 groups. Card locators also included surrounding containers.
findings.nextAction: Select a populated runtime group and scope each card to its actual container; the five representative rechecks passed without skips.

findings.reason: Prerequisite response readers could consume an in-flight response from the previous page and lose its body during navigation.
findings.nextAction: Match requests started by the current navigation and consume their bodies immediately; targeted rerun in progress.

findings.reason: The owned configuration edit submitted capacity 2, checkout 2 and new dates, and returned HTTP 200. Fresh GET data still contains capacity 1, checkout 1 and the original dates.
findings.nextAction: Fix the group/configuration update persistence. Retain the saved-value assertions.

findings.reason: The deployed owned-configuration DELETE returned HTTP 500. The test previously waited for an admin-only endpoint and obscured this response with a timeout; the matcher now accepts the deployed actor-scoped endpoint.
findings.nextAction: Fix the deployed configuration delete handler. Configuration 427 in owned group 385 remains; do not automatically resubmit this failed deletion.

findings.reason: Typing a configuration name or a no-match query leaves unrelated Floating License cards visible. The strengthened checks verify every displayed result, rather than accepting one matching card.
findings.nextAction: Connect the deployed search state to configuration filtering and rerun the unchanged functional assertions.

findings.reason: The actual card or bulk configuration DELETE returned HTTP 500. Cleanup of the disposable parent group returned success but the group remained visible after reload.
findings.nextAction: Fix the Floating License deletion handler and parent-group persistence. Keep the real deletion assertions; inspect the recorded owned leftovers before any further cleanup attempt.

findings.reason: Feature creation returned HTTP 201, but the subsequent version/access-level PUT did not complete within 30 seconds; the fresh cleanup GET also timed out. The update-file upload was not reached.
findings.nextAction: Investigate the unfinished Feature PUT and availability. Do not claim upload/delete coverage or retry the previous mutation blindly.

findings.reason: The required fresh Profile listing returned HTTP 403 before the owned configuration was created. No deletion was attempted in this case.
findings.nextAction: Verify session and endpoint access, then rerun the case with a fresh authenticated session.

findings.reason: Two independent owned-license checks (expiry in seven days, and already expired) persisted enabled licenses in group 1. The Dashboard cutoff query included that group but returned only eight users with last=true and omitted the new user/license. The extension action could not be reached. Owned licenses and users were cleaned up.
findings.nextAction: Investigate the Dashboard users filter/date query and backend pagination. Retain the owned-record discovery assertion; do not substitute an unrelated business license.

findings.reason: The header displays an account identifier rather than the email address explicitly required by the user.
findings.nextAction: Display the signed-in account email in the application header, then rerun this case.

findings.reason: The Edit License icon button has an empty accessible name.
findings.nextAction: Add an accessible Edit License name to the application button.

findings.reason: Cancelling the Edit License dialog does not restore keyboard focus to the invoking Edit action.
findings.nextAction: Restore focus to the original Edit trigger after closing the dialog.

findings.reason: With a disposable user, persisted Hardware ID, assigned Profile/Role and both valid dates, the Dashboard approval sends PUT /api/users and receives HTTP 500. The request is not approved. Cleanup dismisses only the owned request and removes the owned user.
findings.nextAction: Inspect the approval request DTO and backend exception. The observed payload includes a new license id of 0 and a response-only @id field; verify the backend contract rather than altering the test request to hide the application failure.

findings.reason: The Floating Configurations radio selection changes with ArrowLeft, but keyboard focus is lost after the UI updates. The selected Expiration radio remains inactive.
findings.nextAction: Keep the radio group mounted during data refresh or restore keyboard focus to the selected radio after the update; retain the focus assertion.

findings.reason: Clearing the required expiration field and saving an owned license sends PUT /api/users and receives HTTP 201 rather than displaying a required-field validation error. The current client falls back to the previous date.
findings.nextAction: Validate the required expiration before Save and show a field error; do not silently restore the prior value and report success. Keep the owned-license boundary check.

findings.reason: An owned license update succeeds and persists. When the subsequent list refresh is deliberately rejected, the UI does not show a visible refresh error. The controlled failure is limited to reads; the owned update and cleanup use the real server.
findings.nextAction: Surface the failed list refresh and provide a retry path without resubmitting the successful update.

findings.reason: The functional pending-state assertions completed, but Playwright failed while finalizing evidence: unexpected file stream length and a truncated trace ZIP. The recorded result remains failed; a pass is not claimed.
findings.nextAction: Inspect the trace-recording/archiving failure and rerun only after execution is authorized again.

notes: Role lifecycle 2288 reached and verified create, edit, and role deletion after reload; its parent Profile cleanup returned HTTP 500.

Export/download manual-verification exception remains user-authorized. Other skips require genuinely unavailable data.
Profile feature association, removal, and prerequisite role deletion all succeeded and persisted; the parent Profile delete returned HTTP 500.
The 10 repaired Hub user create/update/delete cases passed with zero skips.
